gloss: to crawl out; to creep out

definitions.gloss: to crawl out; to creep out; to emerge by crawling
definitions.explanation: To move out of an enclosed or confined space by crawling. Used for insects, babies, or people in tight spaces. Can also be used figuratively for emerging from a difficult situation.

examples.japanese: {虫|むし}が{穴|あな}から{這|は}い{出|だ}してきた。
examples.english: A bug crawled out of the hole.

examples.japanese: {赤|あか}ちゃんが{布団|ふとん}から{這|は}い{出|だ}した。
examples.english: The baby crawled out from under the blanket.

examples.japanese: {地震|じしん}で{崩|くず}れた{建物|たてもの}の{下|した}から、{生存者|せいぞんしゃ}が{這|は}い{出|だ}してきたときは{皆|みな}{涙|なみだ}を{流|なが}した。
examples.english: Everyone shed tears when survivors crawled out from under the collapsed building after the earthquake.

notes:
USAGE:
A compound verb formed from {這|は}う (to crawl) + {出|だ}す (to come out). Often used with てくる to indicate motion toward the speaker.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {穴|あな}から{這|は}い{出|だ}す (to crawl out of a hole)
- {布団|ふとん}から{這|は}い{出|だ}す (to crawl out of bed)
- {這|は}い{出|だ}してくる (to come crawling out)
